# How this pipeline works

Every workflow here is generated from `hollow.yml`. To change the pipeline, change `hollow.yml` and run `npx the-hollow upgrade`. `npx the-hollow fix` explains a failing run (and repairs it, if you configured a model).

## On every pull request

`ci.yml` runs these jobs, and the `CI passed` check sums them up for branch protection:

- **Build and test:** installs from the lockfile (`python -m pip install --upgrade pip && python -m pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt`), then runs:
  - Lint: `ruff check .`
  - Format check: `ruff format --check .`
  - Test: `pytest`
  - the django migrations, applied to a throwaway database
- **Secret scan:** Gitleaks over the whole git history.
- **Dependency scan:** OSV-Scanner on the lockfiles; fails on high or worse.
- **SAST:** CodeQL on public repos, Semgrep on private ones.
- **Container:** builds the image and scans it with Trivy.

`pr-title.yml` requires a Conventional Commit title, since squash merges turn it into the changelog.

`migrations.yml` (the `Migration safety` check) fails on destructive migrations unless the pull request has the `allow-destructive-migration` label. See docs/migrations.md.

## Releases and deploys

`release.yml` deploys to your server over SSH. Every merge to `main` deploys to staging. release-please keeps a release pull request open; merging it tags a version and promotes the exact build staging ran to production, which waits for approval. Nothing is rebuilt on the way.

Production waits for the `production` environment's required reviewers. Where GitHub offers none (private repos without Enterprise), the release stops before production, and someone with write access approves it by running the Release workflow with the version: `gh workflow run release.yml -f version=v1.2.3`.

| Environment | URL | Deploys |
|---|---|---|
| staging | https://staging.example.com | on every merge |
| production | https://example.com | on release |

After each deploy, the environment's URL plus `/` must answer without a server error within two minutes.

Each deploy applies the database migrations before its new code goes live. See docs/migrations.md.

## Rolling back

A failed health check, or a container that never becomes healthy, puts the previous image back on the server automatically. To roll back by hand, run the Release workflow with an earlier version. Database migrations are not rolled back; see docs/migrations.md.

## Secrets and variables

`npx the-hollow secrets` lists which are set and offers to set the missing ones. Values never go in a file.

| Name | Kind | Where | Needed | What for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `VPS_SSH_KEY` | secret | staging environment | yes | SSH private key the staging deploy uses to reach app.example.com |
| `VPS_KNOWN_HOSTS` | variable | staging environment | yes | app.example.com's SSH host key, so deploys only talk to that server |
| `VPS_SSH_KEY` | secret | production environment | yes | SSH private key the production deploy uses to reach app.example.com |
| `VPS_KNOWN_HOSTS` | variable | production environment | yes | app.example.com's SSH host key, so deploys only talk to that server |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` | secret | repo | yes | Slack incoming webhook URL for failure and recovery alerts |
| `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` | secret | repo | optional | token release-please uses, so CI runs on release pull requests |

## Scheduled checks and incidents

`scheduled.yml` checks staging (https://staging.example.com/), production (https://example.com/) every 15 minutes. GitHub delays scheduled runs when it is busy, and turns off schedules in public repos after 60 days without activity, so treat this as a baseline, not uptime monitoring.

Every night it re-scans the default branch's dependencies, since new vulnerabilities are published without any code changing.

A failing synthetic check, nightly scan or production deploy raises an incident issue labelled `hollow-incident` and a Slack message. Repeats add a comment instead of a new issue, and the issue closes itself once the check passes again.
